articleTitle: Improvement of Thermally Modified Oak Wood Surface Hardness by Ultrasonic Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: In this paper the possibilities of original ultrasonic technology for improving of surface hardness of thermally modified oak (Quercus robur) wood are investigated as decreasing of thermally modified wood mechanical properties and also wood hardness is one of the known disadvantages of this modification method. The machine realizing the proposed treatment technology consists of an ultrasonic module and an infeed system. Effect of two opposite located sonotrodes of ultrasonic module, directly contacting the surface of the lumber when passing through the machine, allows improving its mechanical properties in one pass without any additional operations. It is shown that by this technology surface hardness of thermally modified oak wood timber can be significantly increased up to 1.5 times, that corresponds to the initial values of wood hardness.

articleTitle: Broadband Phased Antenna Array with Quasi-Log-Periodic Microstrip Dipole Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: Modular architecture in RF design is becoming more prominent. Unified subarray elements are commonly used to form the pre-defined aperture in modular passive or active antenna arrays. This paper covers the study of a unified subarray's antenna element operating in a wideband phased antenna array. A quasi-log-periodic dipole antenna with microstrip excitation was used to provide low cross-polarization properties, X-band matching and good capabilities for beam-steering. VSWR, gain, and axial ratio plots are presented.

articleTitle: Features of Control of Condensed Media in Visible Light
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The problems of express control of condensed media using refractometers with an artificial light source are considered. The necessity of control of various media, especially volatile ones, using small-size passive refractometers is substantiated. It is proposed to use a refractometer design that operates with the use of visible light for the express control of condensed media. The advantages of this refractometer design in visible light are noted. The peculiarities of measuring the refractive index of condensed media are established. The results of studies of various condensed media and their analysis are presented. The results of measuring the refractive index are compared with the data obtained with other instruments.

articleTitle: Development of a Programmable Lamp Containing Leds in the Ultraviolet, Visible and Far Red Spectral Ranges for Efficient Plant Growth
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The paper considers the process of creating a programmable LED lamp, which contains LEDs in the UV, visible and far red spectral ranges for the crops germination. The following functions have been added to the software for controlling the lamp: lamp on and off time (time range of operation); number of working days; settings for the internal real-time clock; changing the intensity of the each LED circuit luminescence by day; lamp on/off function from the menu. The device has also been added the ability to record lighting programs.

articleTitle: Laser Cleaning of Painting Layers in Combination with Chemical Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The work examined a fragment of the 18th-century bas-relief (metope) from the courtyard facade of the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts building. As a result, a combined method was developed for cleaning a gypsum bas-relief from surface paint layers using a chemical solvent of dimethyl sulfoxide in combination with laser cleaning technology. Comparative analysis with the area cleaned by the traditional method showed that the area cleaned by the combined cleaning method had a more uniform color without visible surface damage.

articleTitle: Analysis of Thermal Regime of Promising Energy Outputs of W-band High-Power Vacuum Microwave Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: It is essential to guarantee the design's manufacturability, electrical and thermal strength, and mechanical robustness while creating energy outputs in the mm-wavelength range. The dielectric material used for the vacuum-tight energy output diaphragm must have both high thermal conductivity and thermal stability. Oxides of aluminum or beryllium, polycrystalline boron nitride and polycrystalline diamond are mainly used as materials for vacuum-tight diaphragms. The paper presents the results of studying by numerical methods the thermal regime of ceramics made of oxides of aluminum and beryllium, polycrystalline boron nitride and diamond as part of vacuum-tight microwave energy output for mm-range electrovacuum devices (EVD). A comparison of heat-dissipating capacity of various vacuum-tight energy output designs was carried out using various dielectrics. Based on the results of the analysis, a dielectric material was determined combining the necessary electrodynamic and heat-dissipating properties, availability and manufacturability.

articleTitle: Study of Interference Patterns in the Far Field of an Optical Phased Antenna Array with Electro-Optical Control
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: This paper provides a justification for the relevance of the development of non-mechanical laser beam control systems for organizing an inter-satellite optical communication links. Methods of laser beam control are described. Brief theoretical basis for the formation of the radiation pattern of optical phased antenna arrays are given. The radiation patterns of optical phased antenna arrays with radiating elements implemented in the integrated and fiber forms on a lithium niobate crystal and a multicore fiber are studied. An infrared camera was used to record interference patterns in the far zone. The phase delay between the channels was controlled using electro-optical phase shifters. It has been experimentally proven that when voltage is applied to the phase shifters, it is possible to control the position of the peak Of <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf> radiation pattern. This confirms the possibility of using the studied optical phased antenna arrays to control a laser beam in free space optical communication lines.

articleTitle: The Development of a Voltage-Controlled Generator with Digital Tuning for a Multifunctional Radar Station
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The necessity of multifunctional radar station development for solving various tasks, including environmental monitoring, is substantiated. The necessity has been established for solving several tasks, including environmental monitoring of air spaces, scanning the emitted microwave signal frequency in the range from 2 to 18 GHz, with a tuning step of 10 MHz. The emerging radar station problems during the implementation of this range are considered. The disadvantages of analog voltage-controlled generators (VCG), which are used in radar stations to synthesize a grid of microwave frequencies in the range of several GHz, are considered. A digital tuning VCG design has been developed on the domestic component base to implement the synthesis of a microwave frequency grid in the range from 2 to 18 GHz. The main characteristics of the developed VCG are investigated and compared with similar developments of the world's leading manufacturer (Planar Monolithics Industries). The effectiveness of radar station with a developed VCG usage for solving various tasks is shown.

articleTitle: Multi-position MIMO Space SAR Principles and Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The article proposes the concept of a multi-position space SAR. The proposed approach is designed to solve the problems and replace of large SAR based on AESA, to increase the reliability and replaceability of its parts. Each element of the system is a simple transceiver with low output power. A high value of energy is achieved due to the possibility of using medium-sized passive antennas. When sensing, orthogonal code signals are used to ensure the incoherence of the operation of the system parts. Signals are received using MIMO technology.

articleTitle: Creation of an Automated Cultivation System Containing Phyto-illumination of the UV and Visible Ranges of the Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The paper considers the process of creating an automated hydroponic installation with LED lighting in the UV and visible ranges of the spectrum for the germination of agricultural crops. The system implements remote monitoring of microclimate parameters, which include humidity and air temperature, oxygen and carbon dioxide indicators, lighting for effective plant growth. Maintenance of the required operating modes of the installation is automated.

articleTitle: Double Ground Fault Resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: In this paper we present a computation method of resistance between two electrodes buried in the ground. Electrodes have different electric potentials, current flows through the ground form one to another. Resistance is calculated by means of single electrode resistance, obtained formula is verified by finite element simulation of current flow between two electrodes.

articleTitle: MM-Band Reflectarray with Extended Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: A wideband reflectarray operating in 20 GHz-30 GHz band is presented. The proposed antenna is based on multi-resonance reflecting elements consisting of concentric rings. These elements have great phase-shifting range and allow compensation of the frequency dependence of the required phase shift at a distinct point on the reflector. Thus, wide frequency band alongside with high gain is achieved.

articleTitle: A Volumetric Meander-Shaped Strip Microwave Structures as a Conversion Elements of Dielectric Testing Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The paper proposes a new type of transducer elements for dielectric testing devices operating in the long-wavelength region of the microwave range, based on volumetric meander-shaped strip lines. Their main difference is the increased conversion sensitivity and smaller linear dimensions in comparison with sensors based on planar transmission lines. As an approbation of the sensor, built in the form of a meander-shaped volumetric strip structure, the results of assessing the degree of oil watering are given.

articleTitle: Electric Field Optimization of High Voltage Electrode
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the possibilities of using special shaped electrodes to decrease negative impact of fringe effect. Two major papers in the scientific literature on this topic are reviewed. The verification of their results is carried out with help of COMSOL Multiphysics. The electric field uniformity for plane-parallel geometry is confirmed. It is demonstrated that the usage of these electrodes for axisymmetric structures is incorrect. A new method of searching for special shape electrodes based on the principle of curve curvature regulation is described. This algorithm allows us to find contour for disk electrode. Unlike other iterative algorithms, the obtained contour is described by the analytical equation, rather than by an array of coordinates. It means that it can be scaled with unchanged ratio of electrode's thickness to electrode-plane distance.

articleTitle: Shortwave and Infrared Radiation Source for the Skin Pathologies Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The paper considers the problems arising in the application of modern methods of skin cancer detection. The necessity of developing new approaches to the diagnosis of skin pathologies based on photonics and optoelectronics methods is substantiated. A new method of image processing of neoplasms on the basis of an advanced multispectral radiation source with a controlled spectrum in the short-wave, near-ultraviolet and infra-red ranges is proposed. A series of images of a benign neoplasm in the abdominal region were obtained in order to analyse different skin areas, depending on the selected radiation ranges. Conclusions were drawn regarding the necessity of using the short wavelength range to detect pigmentation accompanying the neoplasm, and the infra-red range to detect internal tissue structures of abnormalities. We performed MATLAB Image Processing Toolbox image processing using spatial filtering, histogram equalization and matrix concatenation to minimize irregular skin structures in images. Intensity distribution graphs of images are given, the degree of absorption by skin chromophores in a selected wavelength range is analyzed. Conclusions on necessity of application of the developed method of research of skin pathologies in medicine are made.

Author Keywords: shortwave optical range Digital biomedical image processing

articleTitle: Optics Capabilities for the Implementation of the Next Generation High-Speed Flight Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the important capabilities of optics for the creation of all optical flight control system, such as the capability to build optical sensors and implement logical operations. It concludes with an analysis of the future development of high-speed data processing and control.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Automated Stand for Directivity Pattern Measurements of Small-Sized Aperture Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The results of the development of a low-cost automated setup for measuring the radiation patterns (RP) of small-sized aperture antennas, which makes it possible to carry out an experimental estimation of the RP in the E- and H-planes, are presented. The obtained results of measurements of the RP of dual-reflector antennas with axisymmetric symmetric Cassegrain geometry and a corrugated conical horn are compared with the results of numerical simulation and direct calculation of the RP using the aperture method.

articleTitle: 3D Imaging of Underwater Cultural Heritage
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: At the moment 3D imaging is one of most powerful tools for documenting Cultural Heritage (CH) objects that makes possible their high-precision virtualization and representation. Nowadays this approach is frequently used in a routine base in many museums around the world. Meanwhile, a considerable number of CH objects found in underwater scenarios are documented and restored on site, following the newest trends in the CH preservation field. Our paper is devoted to 3D imaging of underwater CH. We will present overview of state-of art of underwater 3D scanning and photogrammetry. We analyzed features of underwater 3D imaging and mathematical algorithms which are most effective at creation of computing 3D models objects documenting in underwater environment. Preliminary experimental results of underwater 3D imaging also will be presented.

articleTitle: Planar Ultrawideband Antenna with 5.8 GHz ISM Band Rejection
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: In this paper a planar UWB antenna for communication between UAVs is presented. The bandwidth (for VSWR < 2) is 2.1 – 8.6 GHz. The antenna design provides a rejection of the 5.8 GHz ISM band. Various types of slots for filtering out narrow frequency bands are considered. The results of the computer-aided simulation and experimental study of the developed antenna layout are presented.

articleTitle: Restoration of Original Color Appearance of Decorative Iron-Based Metal Artworks by Laser Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: This article is focused on the study of the possibility of the restoration of the lost decorative color appearance of iron-based metal artworks. An ytterbium fiber laser (1064 nm) was used to irradiate carbon steel surfaces. Laser-induced color oxide layers of blue, yellow, brown, and white colors were obtained on the surface of carbon steel by adjusting the main laser radiation parameters: power, repetition rate, beam scanning speed, and pulse duration. In experiments, we used mockups on the surface of which colored oxide layers had been obtained by means of laser treatment. Then we damaged the oxide layers, creating artificial corrosion, and reproduced the original color appearance by means of several stages of laser processing, including cleaning, polishing, and local heating of the mockups' surfaces. The conducted studies show that the application of lasers is a promising method for the reconstruction of the color appearance of iron-based cultural heritage objects.

articleTitle: Full-Metal Fabry-Perot Antenna Array with Bilinear Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: Numerical and experimental results for the antenna array based on a Fabry-Perot resonator of bilinear polarization are presented. The proposed antenna array are design to be manufactured using laser cutting technology and to be operated in 4.8-4.99 GHz frequency band. The manufactured prototype design is all-metal with the exception of square-shaped microstrip radiator made on a polyvinyl chloride substrate.

articleTitle: Metrological Assurance of Laser Measuring Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: Currently laser measuring systems and sets, interferometers and other measuring instruments the principle of which is based on the use of stabilized laser radiation sources are widely used in metrological laboratories of leading enterprises of various industries and in leading scientific institutes. This report substantiates the need for ensuring the traceability of these measuring systems to the State Primary Standard of the unit of length - metre. Also this report describes the methods for transferring the unit of length to laser radiation sources in the range from 500 to 1050 nm.

Author Keywords: State Primery Standart of the unit of length

articleTitle: Optical Properties of Bromine-Doped Perovskite Films
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The optical properties of bromine-doped organic-inorganic perovskite thin layers were investigated. Replacing iodine, which is component of perovskites, with bromine improves film properties due to the formation of a more stable crystal structure. In this study, perovskite films MAPbI2Br, MAPbBr3, FAPbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, FA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,85</inf>Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,15</inf>Pb(I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,85</inf>Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,15</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Cs0,05(FA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>MA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,95</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-y</inf>, were obtained by spin-coating method. To determine the optimal technological parameters, such as the spin-coating speed, annealing time and temperature, we studied the photoluminescence and absorbance spectra of the created films. It was found that the use of an antisolvent leads to an increase in the photoluminescence intensity, which can be attributed to the formation of a better-quality film with fewer defects.

articleTitle: Development of an Autonomous Greenhouse for The Arctic Regions Based on Solar and Wind Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The simulation of a greenhouse for the Arctic regions was carried out, which operates autonomously using solar and wind energy, as well as adapted to low temperatures and capable of producing plant products directly on the territory of the Russia Federation Arctic zone. To develop the project, a comprehensive work was carried out to study all aspects of the greenhouse installation and all the systems necessary for its successful operation, namely: the design of the greenhouse container, the design of the growing rack, the heating system, the irrigation system, the lighting system, the humidification system, the cooling systems, power supply.

Author Keywords: the Arctic zone of the Russian Federation

articleTitle: Formation of Weakly Scattering Intra-Fiber Centers in the Interaction of Powerful Optical Counter Pulses
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: In this paper, we study the process of forming a scattering center in the meeting zone of optical pulses of high power and short duration. The statistical values of the optical radiation power density at which the optical fiber fuse effect occurs are considered. A method for the formation of scattering centers in the fiber core is proposed and theoretically justified. As a result, it was shown that the interaction of counter pulses above the threshold power for an optical fiber can cause scattering centers.

articleTitle: Post-Ablative Treatment with Toluene of Coatings Based on ITO and ITO/CNT for Issues of Liquid-Crystal Electro-Optics
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: In this paper the post-ablative profiles of indium-tin oxides and indium-tin oxides with carbon nanotubes based coatings before and after treatment with the toluene were compared and discussed. For ablation the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser marker with the wavelength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10, 6\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>, processing speed 50 mm/s and power from 6W to 24W with step 3W was used. Toluene was deposited on ablated surfaces under the standard conditions. The influence of toluene on the relief properties was estimated and measured in 1 hour and 3 days after the treatment. Toluene treatment of ITO with CNTs provides the smooth relief reconstruction, thus this technological step makes it possible to extend the architecture and the functionality of liquid crystal based devices.

articleTitle: Photodetectors Based on Colloidal Quantum Dots
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: Currently, colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) have received considerable attention due to their unique properties, such as the ability to control the band gap in a wide range, the tuning of absorption spectra, the possibility of precipitation from solutions, etc. These properties are especially important for research in the field of detection of electromagnetic radiation in the visible and infrared ranges. The paper presents an overview of photodetectors based on colloidal quantum dots lists the most commonly used materials for creating these devices. Technologies for creating efficient and high-speed photodetectors are described. Particular attention is paid to photodetectors based on metal chalcogenides, which are sensitive in the near infrared range. Advantages and disadvantages of photodetectors based on colloidal quantum dots are described. As well as the results of the introduction of CdSe-based CQDs into organic photosensitive structures of the CuPc/PTCDA type are presented.

articleTitle: The Study of Visible LED Radiation Influence on the Growth Characteristics of Lactuca Sativa L
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: LED radiation with the correct spectral composition can significantly increase the nutritional value of cultivated crops. At the same time, it should be borne in mind that each plant needs a certain spectrum at each stage of growth. In the present work, the influence of far-wave and short-wave LED radiation on the growth of lactuca sativa I was studied. The Photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD) values were obtained depending on the pump current and the distance from the source to the radiation receiver. The following ratios of light fluxes of the short-wave and long-wave ranges of the spectrum were used: 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>/0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, 75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>/25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, 50<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>/50<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, 25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>/75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>/100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. We defined optimal ratios of light fluxes to increase the rate of appearance of cotyledons: for 200 µmol.m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>.s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>by samples under illumination modes of 75% red / 25% blue light and 100% red; for 300 µmol.m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>.s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>at 25% red/ 75% blue and 100% red. It has been proven that with an increase in the proportion of the red range of the spectrum, the rate of appearance of the first and second characteristic lactuca sativa l leaves increase. The highest net weight yield and leaf area were achieved with 75% red light and 25% blue light.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Piezoelectric Material Characteristics for Ultrasonic Transducers
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: In the present paper the possibility of using piezoelectrics as a plate emitting and receiving transducers for acoustic sensors of angular motion is analyzed. In contrast to previous studies, in this paper piezoceramic is considered as a transducer material. By numerical estimation and simulation, the specific cut-offs are determined that can be used for effective excitation of various oscillation modes.

articleTitle: Application of Soda Aluminosilicate Glass Doped with Europium and Silver Molecular Clusters in Ion Exchanged Layers as Beam Conversion for Optical Spark Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The spectra of possible sparks and the consequences of the discharge are analyzed. Coordination of optical supplies, photodetector with radiation conversion was carried out. Glass doped with silver molecular clusters and Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ ions was chosen as a transducer for optical sensors. Includes its luminescence spectra, optical density and quantum yield at various excitation wavelengths.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic Characteristics of Promising Energy Outputs of W-band High-Power Vacuum Microwave Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The results of studying electrodynamic characteristics (EDC) of vacuum-tight energy outputs, intended for operation in W-band high-power electrovacuum devices (EVD) are presented. The designs of a pillbox window are considered, in which the formation of an electric field on the surface of a ceramic disk is realized by TE11, TM11 wave types of a round waveguide and the Brewster window, which is a segment of a rectangular waveguide with standard cross-section and an inclined ceramic diaphragm. In the outputs under study the use of ceramics based on oxides of aluminum, beryllium, as well as polycrystalline boron nitride and diamond was considered as a vacuum-tight dielectric diaphragm. A comparison is made of the operating frequency band and losses of the considered vacuum-tight energy output designs when using various dielectrics. On the basis of the obtained EDC, recommendations are given for the choice of ceramics for high-power microwave EVDs.

articleTitle: Development of Optical Sensors Using LED as Photodetector: LED Apogee Detector Example
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The possibility of using LED as optical light detector is argued. The operating principle of the LED apogee detector is discussed in detail. An analysis of the radiation of the sky and the earth was carried out, comparing the data on the absorption intensity of the LED used.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Method for Determining the Liquid Level in an Underground Tank
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: A method for determining the filling level of an underground tank without internal access using ultrasonic waves is proposed. The relationship between the attenuation rate of an acoustic wave during its propagation in the tank wall and the level of the substance inside this tank is considered. This characteristic is supposed to be used to measure the level of a substance in closed containers.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Reproduction of Geometrical Primitives Using Different 3D Printing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: 3D printing techniques are widely used nowadays in different areas, thanks to its replication speed, good accuracy, good material reliability and low cost. Everyday these techniques are applied in new and diverse fields, employed for testing purposes, replication and reconstruction tasks and even to substitute complex and hard to replace mechanical parts. However, there are different methods available in the market with various reproduction accuracy degrees depending on multiple factors like physical properties of the used materials. To evaluate these issues, we used three popular 3D printing technologies (FDM, SLA and SLS) to reproduce geometrical primitives created in CAD software with the goal of evaluating how these different techniques represent important features of these particular figures like hard edges and plain surfaces.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of the Induction System for the Creation of Anticorrosive Coatings on Fasteners
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The article describes the numerical simulation of the induction system of the installation for the creation of anticorrosive coatings based on zinc in an electromagnetic field on fasteners. In order to ensure high efficiency of the heat treatment of the processed products and accelerate the process of thermodiffusion galvanizing, it is necessary to create such conditions that as much Joule heat as possible is generated in the processed products. The work of the system with different retort materials at different frequencies of the electromagnetic field was considered as part of the research. The obtained results of numerical modeling allowed us to draw conclusions about the choice of the optimal frequency of the field for the process and the retort material for loading the mixture for coating on fasteners.

articleTitle: Development of Lighting Techniques for Agricultutal Crops To Create an Energy-Efficient LED Phyto-Lamp
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The necessity of developing methods for seed germination in greenhouses and nurseries to improve the efficiency of planting in the fields is substantiated. Methods of illumination of various agricultural crops have been developed. Based on these techniques, an energy-efficient LED phyto-lamp has been developed, containing a set of five types of LEDs: 365 nm, 440 nm, 520 nm, 660 nm and 730 nm. The influence of different spectral composition of radiation and the tightness of photosynthetic photon concentration on the characteristics of seed growth has been studied. The high seed germination, low hypocotyl elongation, and active root system development were achieved using a combination of different intensities at different wavelengths. It is established that the photon flux density for effective seed germination is about 300 mmol/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.</sup>s.

articleTitle: Dualband 5G Antenna for Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: In this paper, the results of a simulation of a dualband 5G antenna for wireless power transmission using Altair FEKO software are presented. Frequency bands were selected as 4.4-5.0 n 5.15-5.925 GHz, these bands are declared by standard 5G Sub-6 GHz (bands n79 and n46). The construction of the antenna was developed as complex-shaped patch antenna. Research of the main characteristics was made, and also the parameterization task was solved for this antenna by the criterion of minimizing the SWR. Patch has got SWR 1.058 and 1.273 at bands we're studying. At the end, the prototyping of this model was carried out. Experimental studies of the frequency dependence of the SWR of the antenna found out that the results of nature measurement don't confront the results of computer simulation.

articleTitle: Colloidal Quantum Dots in the Photosensitive Layer Based on Perovskite
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: The effect of colloidal quantum dots on the optical characteristics of photosensitive layers of the perovskite crystal structure has been investigated. The study used a comparative analysis of photosensitive layers with and without quantum dots. As a result, absorption, transmission and photoluminescence spectra were obtained. It can be concluded that the inclusion of CQD in the composition of perovskite leads to an increase of absorption and a decrease of transmission in the short-wavelength region from the peak of photoluminescence of quantum dots. It can also contribute to the shift of perovskite photoluminescence peak to the long-wavelength region.

articleTitle: Analysis of Systematic Error of Autocollimating Null Indicator and the Ways to Eliminate It
publicationTitle: 2023 Seminar on Fields, Waves, Photonics and Electro-optics: Theory and Practical Applications (FWPE)
abstract: Dynamic goniometers are among the most precise non-contact optical angle measuring systems, which provide complete measuring process automation. The optical interaction with the test object reflecting faces in these systems is implemented by the null-indicator, which is extremely sensitive device and thus multitude of goniometer error sources are related to it. This article focuses on one specific systematic error typical for dynamic goniometers that utilize null-indicators based on autocollimation principle. This error originates from null-indicator internal components poor adjustment together with certain measurement conditions. Based on the experimental data obtained, the accuracy of the said null indicator was analyzed and the main sources of the systematic errors were identified and possible measure to eliminate those errors were proposed.
